guitar.guitaristsText: Gary Rossington / Allen Collins / Ed King
guitar.modelsText: Gibson Les Paul / Gibson Explorer / Fender Stratocaster
guitar.notes: Confirmed and slightly expanded — Rossington's Les Paul and Collins's Explorer (and King's Strat) are the classic three-guitar lineup; medium is appropriate given multiple guitarists/instruments.

tone.target: bright Southern rock crunch with twangy clean-to-edge breakup
tone.profile: bright Southern rock crunch with twangy clean-to-edge breakup
tone.summary: A clean boost/comp setup feeding into a classic British amp model (UK 45 or UK 50) with a vintage cabinet, emphasizing twangy single-coil tones and controlled breakup.
corrections: lean less blues-rock, more Southern rock

rig.name: Lynyrd Skynyrd - Sweet Home Alabama - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Provide subtle clean boost for twang and bite.
blocks.gap: A dedicated 'Clean Boost' or 'Treble Booster' would be ideal, but the general Boost module works well to lift the upper mids.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the light breakup and grit of a Fender-style tube amp.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is excellent for clean, articulate overdrive, fitting the 'light breakup' requirement perfectly.

blocks.purpose: Add the characteristic 'wah' bite and vocal quality needed for Southern rock.
blocks.gap: None. The V-Wah is versatile enough to provide the necessary filter sweep without sounding overly aggressive.

blocks.purpose: Provide the classic British/American clean-crunch foundation (Fender/Marshall blend).
blocks.gap: The UK 45 is a good proxy for the desired 'Fender/Marshall-ish' sound, offering clarity and punch.

blocks.purpose: Provide a bright, articulate cabinet sound suitable for Southern rock clarity.
blocks.gap: None. This cabinet choice supports the desired 'bright upper mids' and punchy tone.

blocks.purpose: Enhance the upper mids and treble for maximum 'twangy lead bite' and clarity.
blocks.gap: None. Targeted EQ boost is crucial for achieving the specified bright, biting tone.

blocks.purpose: Add subtle width and dimension without sounding like a modern effect (used sparingly).
blocks.gap: The instructions advised avoiding Chorus, but a very low-mix setting is used here to add 'dimension' for double-lead clarity without dominating the tone.

blocks.purpose: Add subtle rhythmic echo for depth and double-lead feel.
blocks.gap: The instructions advised avoiding heavy delay, so settings are kept minimal to provide only a slight sense of space.

blocks.purpose: Provide a natural, dryish room ambience without sounding overly wet or modern.
blocks.gap: None. Room reverb is the best choice for achieving a 'dryish 70s rock feel'.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism and overall vintage punch by upgrading the IR to better capture 70s Southern rock grit.

proposals.reason: The current IR is too clean; a vintage speaker cabinet will add necessary grit and punch for Southern rock.
